public_rationale: The forecast was that AGI would not arrive in 2025, and that deadline has passed. The International AI Safety Report (February 2026) assessed frontier AI through November 2025. It found abilities were 'jagged': systems still failed some simple tasks, were less reliable on multi-step work, and were limited in reasoning about the physical world. The ARC Prize organisers described 2025 as 'progress towards AGI', with a top competition score of 24% on ARC-AGI-2. In October 2025, Microsoft's filing described AGI as not yet declared. The main counterpoint is Altman's informal December 2025 remark that 'AGI kinda went whooshing by', but no system was verified or widely accepted as AGI. On the plain reading, the forecast held.
limitations: AGI is undefined, so the outcome depends on a plain reading: a system widely recognised as general human-level AI.
The ARC evidence covers one benchmark under compute limits.
Altman's informal year-end remark could be read by some as claiming AGI arrived.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AGI will not be achieved in 2025.

statement.excerpt: Gary Marcus stands by his prediction that we will not see AGI in 2025, and regrets that Elon Musk didn’t take his million dollar bet.
statement.document_title: Breaking news: AGI is not imminent!

our_interpretation: Marcus gave no definition of AGI here. The plain reading is that no AI system would be built or shown in 2025 that is generally recognised as AGI: matching human general ability across most cognitive tasks, including new problems, reliably.

A loose remark by an industry figure that AGI may already have happened does not count as AGI being achieved. What would count is a system widely accepted as AGI, a formal declaration such as the one under the Microsoft-OpenAI agreement, or clear human-level general performance in independent evaluations.
The Musk bet remark is context, not a separate testable claim.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from late 2025 or early 2026 that leading AI systems still fell short of general human-level ability (for example, independent assessments showing uneven, 'jagged' abilities and failures on simple tasks, unsolved general-reasoning benchmarks, and no formal AGI declaration), and no system widely accepted as AGI by 31 December 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system released or shown in 2025 that is widely accepted as AGI by independent experts, or a formal, verified declaration of AGI made during 2025.

evidence.excerpt: The capabilities of these systems are ‘jagged’: they can perform many complex tasks but still struggle with some seemingly simpler ones. For example, they are less reliable when projects involve many steps; they still sometimes generate text that includes false statements (‘hallucinations’); they are still limited on tasks that involve interacting with or reasoning about the physical world
evidence.locator: section 'Performance remains uneven across tasks and domains'
evidence.publisher: International AI Safety Report (chaired by Yoshua Bengio)
evidence.explanation: An independent international expert review covering frontier AI through November 2025 found that leading systems still failed at some simple tasks and were limited in multi-step work and physical-world reasoning. That is not general human-level ability.

evidence.excerpt: ARC Prize 2025 demonstrated continued open-source progress towards AGI, with the top Kaggle score reaching 24% on ARC-AGI-2
evidence.explanation: The benchmark organisers describe 2025 as 'progress towards AGI', not arrival: the best competition entry scored 24%, far below the 85% Grand Prize threshold. This is one benchmark, under compute limits, so it is supporting rather than decisive.

evidence.excerpt: If Microsoft uses OpenAI’s IP to develop AGI, prior to AGI being declared, the models will be subject to compute thresholds; those thresholds are significantly larger than the size of systems used to train leading models today.
evidence.publisher: Microsoft (8-K exhibit 99.2, via Boardroom Alpha mirror)
evidence.explanation: In late October 2025, Microsoft and OpenAI described AGI as not yet declared and set up an independent panel to verify any future declaration. This shows that the leading lab had made no formal AGI claim by then.

evidence.excerpt: “AGI kinda went whooshing by… okay fine, we built AGIs”
evidence.explanation: Records an informal December 2025 remark by Altman suggesting AGI had passed. It is a loose, unverified remark, not a demonstrated or verified system, and the same timeline notes he later called a similar claim 'spiritual', not literal. So it does not meet the contradiction condition.
